english.title: Aid / abet the removal of the whole / part of a dog's tail
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) aided, abetted, counselled and procured the removal of the whole or part of a dog's tail for a purpose otherwise than for the animal's medical treatment
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(1)(a) and 32(1) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 and section 44 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980.

english.notes:
(i) Section 6(3) of the Act provides that this offence does NOT APPLY if the dog is a certified working dog that is not more than 5 days old.
(ii) See section 6(4) to (7) for an explanation of the term "working dog", conditions and a defence.
(iii) See section 33 for privation orders.
(iv) See section 34 for disqualification from owning keeping animals.
(v) See section 35 for power to seize animals in connection with disqualification.
(vi) See section 37 for destruction in the interests of the animal.
(vii) See section 40 for the forfeiture of equipment used.
(viii) The maximum penalty for this offence has increased from 29th June 2021; for offences before that date see H7959/AW06006B.

other.timelimitforprosecutions: Complex see section 31 of the Act
other.penalty:
Either way -

Summary: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Note
Section 32(4A) of the Animal Welfare Act 2006 provides that in relation to an offence committed before the commencement of paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 2 to the Sentencing Act 2020, the reference to 12 months is to be read as a reference to 6 months.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex see legislation
